per_view.front: The full original connected complex and base fit the view. The 27 light gray-blue upper-front backings are visually distinguishable from neutral chamfered reveals; lower two rows, projecting entrance frame, side wing and court remain neutral. The improvement is localized and readable, not a full-color facade claim.
per_view.elevation: Only the upper three rows show pane color, each wholly within the original recessed backing. The asymmetric widths/offsets and neutral stone bevels remain legible. Both lower rows remain gray; no sharp artificial color partition across a single triangle.
per_view.rear: Court-facing wings, actual open-gallery representations, bridge and simplified stair towers remain neutral. No transparent/glass color is spread across open corridor slots or louvers.
per_view.side: All similar-looking side window rows and surrounding wall remain neutral. The -Y selection is not mirrored around the corner or extended to the sports-field elevation.
per_view.top: Roof surfaces, roof boxes, court ground, bridge and all horizontal caps remain neutral. No added roof equipment or false glass court closure. Complete original model fits the frame.

visual_review.mono_comparison: Same delivery scene/camera/light/render settings, only temporary material indices reset to neutral without saving scene. Actual front versus this baseline makes the upper window backs lighter/cooler and distinct from the sloped stone reveals. The comparison is not a historical original preview. No need to enlarge scope or darken panes to manufacture more coverage.
source_alignment: YLUS01 and YLUS06 show the targeted front asymmetric chamfered windows, with light glazing/curtains and aluminum framing behind opaque stone reveals. A light low-saturation gray-blue backing proxy is reasonable; uniformly black or neon blue glazing would not be.
YLUS02 shows other teaching/administrative elevations with exposed louvers and distinct window systems; not used to extend the front mask.
YLUS04/05/07 prove open courtyard galleries and bridges. Keeping these neutral avoids false glazing. YLUS03 is an interior stair photograph, not evidence for coloring exterior tower walls as wood.
visual_review.color_interpretation: #98ABB2 is an opaque, uncalibrated glazing/curtain proxy, not transparent glass simulation or a measured glass tint. #AAA79F means neutral/unconfirmed structure, not a claim that all walls share that actual color.
visual_review.framing: Five complete 1200×1200 images individually inspected; independent projection confirms all original vertices inside each orthographic frame.
